place.en: North Africa and the western Mediterranean
place.pt: North Africa and the western Mediterranean

stages.name: Other peoples
stages.desc: Iberians, Celtiberians and other peoples outside the struggle

stages.name: Massyli
stages.desc: Eastern Numidians; from 203 BC Masinissa's united kingdom

stages.name: Masaesyli
stages.desc: Western Numidians, the kingdom of Syphax

stages.name: Carthaginian
stages.desc: Carthage's own territory and subject towns

stages.name: Taken from Carthage
stages.desc: Carthaginian land seized by Masinissa's Numidia

stages.name: Mauri
stages.desc: The Moorish kingdom beyond the Moulouya river

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The Mauri kingdom west of the Moulouya river, a land of horsemen and small towns
King Baga gives Masinissa four thousand Mauri horsemen to escort him home

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberian, Turdetanian and Celtiberian peoples; Phoenician Gades on the Atlantic coast
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades and begins Carthage's conquest of southern Spain
Masinissa commands Numidian cavalry for Carthage in Spain
After Ilipa Carthage loses Spain; Rome holds the south and east coasts

states.name: Libya
timeline: The Emporia of Tripolitania (Lepcis, Oea, Sabratha) pay tribute to Carthage; the Garamantes hold the desert
Lepcis is said to pay Carthage a talent a day; Masinissa claims the Emporia
Masinissa seizes the Emporia; Rome rules for him and Carthage pays five hundred talents

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage's heartland: the city, the farms of Cape Bon, the Medjerda valley and the Sahel ports
Carthage crushes the Mercenary War and reasserts its rule over the Libyan countryside
Scipio lands near Utica; Masinissa joins him
Hannibal is defeated at Zama
Masinissa begins to claim Carthaginian land; Rome leaves the disputes unresolved
Carthage complains that Masinissa has seized over seventy towns and forts in two years
Masinissa takes the Great Plains and the fifty towns of Tusca
Carthage fights Masinissa without Rome's consent and loses an army
Rome's army lands at Utica and lays siege to Carthage

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome rules Italy and, since 241 BC, Sicily
Rome seizes Sardinia from Carthage
Hannibal invades Italy
Hannibal is recalled to Africa
Syphax dies a prisoner at Tibur

states.name: Algeria
timeline: The Masaesyli hold most of the land from the Moulouya eastward; the Massyli of King Gaia hold only the east, around Cirta
Syphax, king of the Masaesyli, allies with Rome; Gaia's young son Masinissa beats him for Carthage
Syphax conquers the Massyli, drives Masinissa into exile and rules from Cirta
Masinissa captures Syphax and takes Cirta; Scipio hails him as king
The peace with Carthage confirms Masinissa as king of Numidia and Rome's ally
Masinissa dies at about ninety; Scipio Aemilianus divides power among three of his sons

events.title: Mercenary War
events.text: Unpaid veterans of the First Punic War and Libyan subjects revolt and besiege Carthage from Tunis.

events.title: Medracen
events.text: A great round royal tomb near Batna shows the wealth of Numidian kings in the third century BC.

events.title: Naravas
events.text: A young Numidian noble, Naravas, deserts the rebels with two thousand horsemen to join Hamilcar Barca.

events.title: Masinissa is born
events.text: Masinissa, son of Gaia, king of the Massyli, is born around this year.

events.title: Sardinia seized
events.text: Rome takes Sardinia from a Carthage exhausted by the Mercenary War.

events.title: Hamilcar in Spain
events.text: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades to build a new empire in Spain.

events.title: Hannibal marches
events.text: Hannibal leaves New Carthage for Italy with Numidian horsemen in his army.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal destroys a Roman army; his Numidian cavalry rides down the fleeing Romans.

events.title: Syphax turns to Rome
events.text: Syphax, king of the Masaesyli, allies with Rome; Roman officers train his infantry.

events.title: First victory
events.text: The young Masinissa leads Carthaginian and Massylian troops and defeats Syphax.

events.title: The Scipios fall
events.text: Masinissa's horsemen help destroy the armies of the brothers Publius and Gnaeus Scipio.

events.title: New Carthage falls
events.text: Young Publius Cornelius Scipio storms Carthage's Spanish capital.

events.title: Massiva freed
events.text: After Baecula, Scipio sends home Masinissa's captured nephew with gifts.

events.title: Ilipa
events.text: Scipio defeats the last Carthaginian army in Spain.

events.title: A secret meeting
events.text: Near Gades, Masinissa meets the Romans and pledges to change sides.

events.title: Scipio visits Syphax
events.text: Scipio and Carthage's Hasdrubal Gisco are guests of Syphax at Siga at the same time.

events.title: Gaia dies
events.text: Gaia's death sets off a civil war over the Massylian throne.

events.title: Mauri escort
events.text: King Baga of the Mauri lends Masinissa four thousand horsemen to ride home.

events.title: Sophonisba
events.text: Hasdrubal Gisco marries his daughter Sophonisba to Syphax, who joins Carthage.

events.title: Exile
events.text: Driven out by Syphax and left for dead, Masinissa hides with a few riders near the Lesser Syrtis.

events.title: Scipio lands
events.text: Scipio's army lands near Utica; Masinissa joins him with a small band of horsemen.

events.title: Ambush at Salaeca
events.text: Masinissa lures Carthaginian cavalry into a trap; their commander Hanno is killed.

events.title: Camps burned
events.text: At night Scipio and Masinissa set fire to the camps of Hasdrubal and Syphax.

events.title: Great Plains
events.text: Scipio and Masinissa defeat the rebuilt armies of Carthage and Syphax.

events.title: Syphax captured
events.text: Syphax is taken in battle; Cirta opens its gates to Masinissa.

events.title: Death of Sophonisba
events.text: Masinissa marries Sophonisba; when Scipio claims her as a captive, she takes poison.

events.title: Hannibal returns
events.text: Recalled after fifteen years in Italy, Hannibal lands at Hadrumetum.

events.title: Zama
events.text: Scipio defeats Hannibal; Masinissa's cavalry helps encircle the Carthaginian infantry.

events.title: Peace of 201
events.text: Carthage gives up its fleet, pays ten thousand talents over fifty years and may not make war without Rome.

events.title: Syphax dies
events.text: The captive Syphax dies in Italy, at Tibur.

events.title: Hannibal flees
events.text: Hounded by his enemies and Rome, Hannibal escapes by sea from his coastal estate.

events.title: Emporia dispute
events.text: Masinissa claims the rich coast of the Lesser Syrtis; Rome's envoys leave the case undecided.

events.title: Grain for Rome
events.text: Masinissa sends grain, horsemen and elephants to Rome's war against Antiochus.

events.title: Seventy towns
events.text: Carthaginian envoys tell the Senate Masinissa has seized over seventy towns and forts in two years.

events.title: Emporia seized
events.text: Masinissa takes the coastal towns; Rome rules for him and Carthage pays five hundred talents.

events.title: Cato in Carthage
events.text: Sent to arbitrate, Cato sees Carthage prosperous and starts demanding its destruction.

events.title: Tusca taken
events.text: Masinissa seizes the Great Plains and the fifty towns of the Tusca district.

events.title: Partisans banished
events.text: Carthage expels about forty supporters of Masinissa; they flee to him.

events.title: Debt paid
events.text: Carthage makes the last of its fifty annual payments to Rome.

events.title: Masinissa's last battle
events.text: Masinissa, aged about eighty-eight, traps Hasdrubal's army; the starving Carthaginians surrender and are cut down.

events.title: Rome declares war
events.text: Utica goes over to Rome; Carthage hands in its weapons, then refuses to abandon the city.

events.title: Siege begins
events.text: Carthage rearms and beats back the first Roman assaults on its walls.

events.title: Masinissa dies
events.text: Masinissa dies at about ninety; Scipio Aemilianus divides his powers among three sons.

chartNote: Share of the area of six modern countries (regions are today's boundaries), each coloured by the power that held its settled coast and hills. A deliberate simplification: Algeria held two Numidian kingdoms until 203 BC, Rome held only part of Spain, Carthage's own losses were small districts, and the vast Saharan areas of Algeria and Libya swing the shares.
